sentences.text:
In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No(S). /2025
 (Arising out of SLP(Crl.) No(s). 5673/2025)
 Shyam Hemantbhai Rajani APPELLANT(s)
 Versus
 State Of Gujarat RESPONDENT(s)
O R D E R Leave granted.
This appeal challenges the order dated 30.01.2025 passed by the High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad in R/Criminal Misc. Application (For Regular Bail-After Charge-sheet) No. 23764 of 2024.

entities.text: High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The appellant herein has been booked for the crime registered pursuant to FIR No.
11208035240307/2024, dated 19.04.2024, lodged with Gandhigram Police Station, District Rajkot for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 495, 323, 504 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC for short).
The appellant preferred an application before the High Court seeking regular bail.
The said application for regular bail has been rejected by the High Court vide impugned order dated 30.01.2025.
Hence, the instant appeal has been preferred.
This Court vide its order dated 17.04.2025, issued notice in the instant matter.

We have heard learned senior counsel in support of the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent-State, and perused the material on record.
Learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that the charges against the appellant herein are under Sections 495, 323, 504, 376(2)(n) and Section 114 of the IPC.
The main charge is that the appellant had earlier married and concealed this fact from the complainant.
However, this fact was known to the complainant when she married the appellant herein.
He further submitted that the parents and sister of the appellant had been granted bail but the appellant has been in jail since the last one year.
Hence, similar relief may be granted to the appellant herein by setting aside the impugned order.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent- State with reference to his counter affidavit contended that there are criminal antecedents against the appellant herein and the charges have not been framed owing to non-cooperation from the parents and sister of the appellant who have been granted bail inasmuch as they are not appearing before the Court and hence, there is a delay in the very framing of the charges.
In the circumstances, he submitted that there is no merit in this appeal.
Considering the circumstances on record, in our view, the case for bail is made out.

We, therefore, allow this appeal and set aside the order passed by the High Court dated 30.01.2025 and direct as under:
The appellant shall be produced before the concerned Trial Court as early as possible and the Trial Court shall release him on bail, subject to such conditions as it may deem appropriate to impose to ensure his presence in the proceedings arising out of FIR No. 11208035240307/2024 mentioned above
It is directed that the appellant shall extend complete cooperation in the ensuing trial.
The appellant shall not misuse his liberty and shall not in any way influence the witnesses or tamper with the material on record.
With the aforesaid directions, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.

,J.
( B.V. NAGARATHNA ) ,J.
( SATISH CHANDRA SHARMA ) NEW DELHI;
